The student must convert the length and the remainder of the wire into the dimensions of two different shapes, including the circle radius from circumference and the 2:1 rectangle, then add the areas. This needs more setup than a single-shape area but little algebraic manipulation.

content.prompt: A length of wire is cut into 2 pieces, one of length $x$ cm. Each piece is bent into a shape.

children.label: a
children.prompt: A 60 cm length of wire is cut into 2 pieces. The piece of length $x$ cm is bent into a square and the other piece into a circle. Show that the total area is given by $A=\dfrac{x^2}{16}+\dfrac{(60-x)^2}{4\pi}$.

answer.worked:
The square has perimeter $x$, so its side is $\dfrac{x}{4}$ and its area is $\dfrac{x^2}{16}$.
The circle has circumference $60-x$:
$$\begin{align*}2\pi r&=60-x\\r&=\frac{60-x}{2\pi}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{circle}}&=\pi\left(\frac{60-x}{2\pi}\right)^2\\A_{\text{circle}}&=\frac{(60-x)^2}{4\pi}\end{align*}$$
$$A=\frac{x^2}{16}+\frac{(60-x)^2}{4\pi}\text{ cm}^2$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: A 90 cm length of wire is cut into 2 pieces. The piece of length $x$ cm is bent into a square and the other piece into a rectangle whose length is twice its width. Show that the total area is given by $A=\dfrac{x^2}{16}+\dfrac{(90-x)^2}{18}$.

answer.worked:
The square has side $\dfrac{x}{4}$, so its area is $\dfrac{x^2}{16}$.
Let the rectangle have width $w$ and length $2w$. Its perimeter is $90-x$:
$$\begin{align*}6w&=90-x\\w&=\frac{90-x}{6}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{rectangle}}&=w(2w)\\A_{\text{rectangle}}&=2\left(\frac{90-x}{6}\right)^2\\A_{\text{rectangle}}&=\frac{(90-x)^2}{18}\end{align*}$$
$$A=\frac{x^2}{16}+\frac{(90-x)^2}{18}\text{ cm}^2$$
